correctness.rationale: For identical unit utilities an EF full allocation necessarily partitions nq goods into bundles of q. Each mixed induced bundle is K_{j,q-j}; a radius-one dominating vertex exists precisely for j=1 or q-1, whereas any 1<=j<=q-1 is covered by one radius-two vertex or two radius-one vertices. Counting labeled class assignments yields N11=binom(n,t)a!b!/((q-1)!)^n for integer t=(a-n)/(q-2) in [0,n], and N12=N21=a!b![x^a](sum_{j=1}^{q-1}x^j/(j!(q-j)!))^n. For q=4,a=b=2n parity makes t=n/2; dividing coefficients reduces to the centered -1,0,1 walk with probabilities 2/7,3/7,2/7 and variance 4/7. Its span-one Fourier local CLT with the central binomial Stirling estimate gives ratio (4/sqrt7)(4/7)^n. These arguments cover q=3, arbitrary positive a,b, boundary t=0,n and even-subsequence restriction; direct n=3 K6,6 count 0 vs 29,700 corroborates finite case.
